prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals

Economy, tax, jobs, business
- Eliminate the deficit and move into surplus; no rises in VAT, Income Tax or National Insurance; raise the Personal Allowance to £12,500 and the higher-rate threshold to £50,000; crack down on tax evasion/avoidance; permanent Office of Tax Simplification; major review of business rates.
- Create 2 million more jobs and 3 million apprenticeships; aim for the highest employment rate in the G7; NIC relief for under‑21s and apprentices; cut £10bn of red tape; expand Start Up Loans; increase SME access to procurement; boost exports.

Infrastructure and digital
- Over £100bn for infrastructure: HS2/HS3, rail electrification, Crossrail 1 and plans for Crossrail 2; freeze regulated rail fares; £15bn for roads and junctions; support cycling and ultra‑low emission vehicles.
- Superfast broadband to 95% by end‑2017 and wider ultrafast rollout; improve mobile coverage to 90% of landmass; prepare for 5G.

Welfare, families, childcare
- Tax‑free childcare (up to £2,000 per child); 30 hours of free childcare for working parents of 3–4 year‑olds.
- Reduce the household benefit cap to £23,000; freeze most working‑age benefits for two years (with exemptions); roll out Universal Credit; a Youth Allowance with work/training requirements; enhanced mental health support; treatment‑linked support for some long‑term but treatable conditions.

Housing
- Extend Help to Buy (including a Help to Buy ISA); build 200,000 discounted Starter Homes for under‑40s and 275,000 additional affordable homes; extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants with replacement; prioritise brownfield, protect the Green Belt; promote self/custom build and locally led garden towns.

Education and skills
- Protect per‑pupil funding; tougher primary standards with resits; expand academies and free schools; intervene in failing/coasting schools; focus on English Baccalaureate subjects.
- Recruit more maths/physics teachers; expand University Technical Colleges and degree apprenticeships; remove cap on university places; introduce postgraduate loans; strengthen SEN and adoption; online age‑verification for pornography.

Health and social care
- Increase NHS funding in real terms, including at least £8bn extra by 2020; move to 7‑day GP and hospital services; integrate health and social care; cancer strategy and drugs fund; enforce mental health access/wait standards; dementia plan; cap residential care costs; digital access to health records; prevention programmes (e.g., diabetes).

Immigration
- Reduce net migration; reform EU welfare access and social housing eligibility; stronger deportation and enforcement; maintain cap on skilled non‑EU visas; student visa reforms and exit checks; landlord status checks; tougher action on illegal working; English‑language requirement for public‑facing roles; Controlling Migration Fund.

Energy and environment
- Increase competition and install smart meters by 2020; insulate 1m more homes; expand nuclear and gas and support renewables that offer value for money; end new subsidies for onshore wind with local consent decisive; support shale with community benefits and a northern wealth fund; meet climate targets.
- Create a “Blue Belt” of marine protections; invest in flood defences; plant 11m trees; protect forests; improve air and water; strengthen animal welfare and tackle illegal wildlife trade.

Crime, justice, security
- Continue police reform and technology adoption; bolster cyber‑crime capability; ban new psychoactive substances; modernise prisons; enact a Victims’ Law; strengthen measures against violence against women and girls; replace the Human Rights Act with a British Bill of Rights; update communications data powers; new powers against extremist groups and speakers.

Defence, foreign policy, aid, EU
- Maintain regular Army at or above 82,000; renew the nuclear deterrent; fund a £160bn equipment plan (including two aircraft carriers); expand reserves to 35,000; uphold NATO commitments.
- Hold an in/out EU referendum by end‑2017 after renegotiation; protect non‑euro members’ interests; pursue major trade deals.
- Maintain 0.7% of national income for aid focused on health, education, water/sanitation, gender equality and crisis response.

Governance, devolution, society and culture
- Further devolution across the UK and English votes for English laws; boundary reforms and anti‑fraud measures; more digital, transparent government.
- Expand National Citizen Service; three days’ paid volunteering for public‑sector and large‑company employees.
- Keep free entry to national museums; freeze the TV licence fee pending charter review; support creative industries and local media.
